applies_why: The judge text evaluates a chain-against-chain collision and faults the challenger's chain for not naming Joseph explicitly.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side. A link is judged by its support, never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word; and a verse whose words leave the question open decides nothing by itself.
room: never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word: read narrowly as only barring a contrary-wording test, or broadly as barring any explicit-naming requirement; I weighed 'does not name Joseph' under the broad reading.
why: The judge calls the challenger's chain footed but then faults it for not naming Joseph, which applies a word-for-word stating-verse test instead of weighing the chain solely by footing.
